newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil exports decline 1.6 pct in June-Nov - paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil exports decline 1.6 pct in June-Nov - paper.

text.p: Brazilian exports declined 1.6 percent and imports grew 14 percent from June to November of this year, prompting officials to consider further measures to slow a growing trade gap, Jornal do Brasil said.

The paper said Brazil's Planning Ministry, which released the figures in a report on Thursday, was preparing another export-promotion package aimed at improving the nation's trade balance, which is expected to end the year with a deficit of close to $5 billion.
Jornal do Brasil did not say what measures the government was considering, although in the past it has offered tax cuts to export sectors.
The government blamed the decline in exports during the six-month period on falling prices for coffee and semi-manufactured goods like cellulose, aluminum and soy oil, the paper said.
It attributed the fast-paced growth of imports to Brazil's steady economic recovery in the second half.
For the January to November period, the ministry reported export growth of 3.1 percent and import growth of 2.5 percent, Jornal do Brasil said.

The more balanced January to November figures reflect a 10 percent growth in exports and an 8.3 percent decline in imports in the January to May period, when the economy was stagnant, the newspaper said.
